name: Linking an app to a website
plain: Proves the app and website are owned together, enabling app links and shared passwords.
meaning: Domain verification file on the website, not a user prompt. Also feeds password autofill.

android.permission: None; autoVerify intent filter plus assetlinks.json
android.prompt_ui: None; user can change in Settings
android.note: Verified at install; Android 12 tightens link handling

ios.prompt_ui: None; Settings per app link toggle
ios.note: Apple CDN caches the file; iOS 14 added swcd checks

limits.headline: Can open web links in the app and offer saved passwords once linked
limits.user_action: Nothing at install. You later tap a web link or a password field
can: Open web links from that company directly in its app
Offer your saved website passwords inside the app
Hand off what you were doing between your devices (iPhone)
cannot: Link to a site that has not published a matching proof file
Show a prompt; you can only turn link opening off in Settings
See your saved passwords without you picking one
limits.reach_label: One check at install, then per link
limits.differs: iPhone has a per link switch in Settings. Android 12 and later lets you change link handling per app.

story.what_it_is: A secret handshake that proves an app and a website belong to the same company.

marketing.name: Associated Domains
marketing.pitch: Lets your app and website share links and saved passwords once you prove you own both.

marketing.name: Verify Android App Links
marketing.pitch: Prove your site and app are linked so web links open straight in the app.

story.for_you: You never see a prompt. You just notice that tapping a link opens the right app, and that your saved password pops up for both the app and the website.
story.for_makers: Makers publish a small file on their website that says 'this app is ours'. That unlocks links that open in the app, shared password autofill and sign in handoff, and it keeps look-alike apps from hijacking links.

use_cases.example: You tap an Amazon link in a text message and the Amazon app opens on that exact product instead of a web page.
A friend sends an Instagram post link and it opens in the Instagram app, already logged in.
Your bank's app shows your saved login suggestion because the phone knows the app and bank.com are the same company.
A friend's invite link for a mobile match opens the game lobby directly, so you join the party in one tap.
A shared trip link opens Uber on the live map so a friend can follow your ride.
The phone refuses to open a fake app that tries to catch links meant for a real bank, because it cannot show the handshake file.

risks: Hidden link between app and site
story.android_note: Android checks the file when the app installs and can open verified links without asking.
story.ios_note: iOS caches the file through Apple's servers and also uses it for shared password autofill.
